title: Oregon OSHA — Cascade Specialty Chemicals

must.line: at least three of the plan's own open gaps carried as findings, in the reading's own terms. The gaps are READ from document_gaps for the current scan, never typed: the four keyword pairs this check used to carry were Haiku's, and the real model's reading has seven gaps in different words.
the plan as stale, as of February 2021
the forklift logs as on file
alarm testing or maintenance records as a finding against the plan's Section 2 condition
the powered industrial truck training records on file, with R. Patel stale: next evaluation due 2026-05-19 and nothing after 2023-05-19 recorded (spec 09 AUDIT USE)
the 42 against 65 contradiction, naming both documents: 42 as of 2021-02-01 from the plan (confirmed) against 65 for 2025 from the 300A (only proposed) (spec 10 AUDIT USE; spec 12 line C4)
the fire extinguisher certificate as stale, the annual maintenance expired 2026-08-20, passed at the run date (spec 11 AUDIT USE; spec 13 line 5)

must_not.line: no finding claiming a fault in the plan that the reading did not find. The allowed words are the plan's own open gaps and its own conditions, read live; only state words that belong to no row are listed here.

acceptable.line: the supplier SDS named as not judged
the forklift log's own gaps carried — read from document_gaps for the current scan, not from the word "horn", which was one model's phrasing of one of them.

agency_was: Run 1b, on Haiku, produced "U.S. Department of Labor - Occupational Safety and Health Administration" for this regulator and no Oregon OSHA row survived, so the case had to follow the label to be measurable at all. The real-model pass on 29 September (claude-opus-5-5) produced "Oregon OSHA" for all six OSHA documents, which is both the spec's string and the correct one for a state-plan state. Recorded, not merged: the same regulator has now been named two ways by two models, and which string a company ends up with is the model's choice, not the product's.
